title: Reject FFM fields before they alias another instance
head: bb40866a7747ffbf2c95021b22ab6b4f488d20d1
body:
### Description

FFM field positions are flattened across the whole batch before bounds are checked. An out-of-range field can therefore land in another training instance: with `field_count=4`, a field numbered 5 on the first row becomes field 1 on the second row. The same input is rejected with batch size 1 but silently changes another example with batch size 2.

Validate each zero-based field index against `field_count` before adding the instance offset. Keep the existing global consistency check and preserve valid sparse fields, repeated fields, empty feature rows, values and ordering.

Fixes #2472.

### Validation

[Independent before/after validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43910433462) checks exact head `bb40866a7747ffbf2c95021b22ab6b4f488d20d1` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- Unchanged FFM and xDeepFM suites: **27 passed** in both environments.
- New cases against unchanged staging: **8 failed, 5 passing controls**.
- Patched full FFM and xDeepFM suites: **40 passed** in both environments, with no skipped tests.
- Six loader cases expose forward and backward aliasing across three records.
- Two native xDeepFM training cases reject the malformed input before any optimizer update; model parameters remain unchanged.
- Five valid-data controls compare complete predictions and gradients across single-record and three-record batches for the linear, FM, CIN, DNN and combined paths. They include empty rows, repeated and unsorted fields, signed feature values and the largest valid field.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 also passes all 40 tests.

### History review

Reviewed 1,497 pre-existing upstream PR heads and 69 fork branches. The current FFM dataset and its former TensorFlow iterator/cache implementations contain 24 distinct reachable source versions across 168 commits; none checks the field against its own instance before flattening. Existing batch-size handling does not address this cross-record aliasing.

### Checklist

- [x] Contribution guidelines and code style followed.
- [x] Regression tests extend the existing FFM and xDeepFM test modules.
- [x] Commit includes the required `Signed-off-by` trailer.
- [x] Targets `staging`.
